answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity work bond that a new key cannot inherit: admission needs fresh proof-of-work whose difficulty scales with the account's age and stake, so every puppet pays the full marginal cost of compute plus a separate deposit. Rewards are concave, so splitting capital dilutes yield. A rational attacker breaks even long before any puppet can wander into a vote. The fragile ledge is reused solutions, so the nonce binds to the address, forcing a unique vertex per identity.
